change: A bounded component walker follows symlinks before consuming remaining dots/parents, checks each traversed directory and search mode, and accepts forty symlink traversals before ELOOP. Recursive mkdir shares that link budget.
Absolute filesystem joins preserve traversal components. Batch parent creation, built-in shell paths, executable lookup and WASI no longer lexically erase them before kernel lookup.

WASI retains its existing lexical descriptor floor check and checks the kernel-resolved path against the descriptor base. Root and scoped descriptor accesses are exercised by the native Cargo-built guest.
Recursive listing retains a usable logical root, including parent components. Namespace mutations reject trailing symlinks as directories; directory metadata consumes the requested trailing slash.
Lexical normalization remains the owner for persisted manifest validation, virtual filenames and relative ESM URL names. No persisted format or migration changes.
Pending pieces borrow request/manifest strings; one prefix buffer is extended/truncated during traversal. No per-piece String copy or candidate-prefix allocation is needed.
coverage: Read/stat identity through symlink followed by parent, recursive batch writes and subsequent reads at the physical path
Recursive directory results can be read/stat-ed through their returned logical paths
Built-in shell reads and actual WASI std::fs reads/writes follow physical parents
Direct JavaScript file execution uses filesystem traversal; ESM imports preserve lexical URL normalization in the same setup
Python open and pinned os.path.realpath agree on the physical file
A native WASI directory descriptor denies an existing external file after symlink/parent traversal with ENOTCAPABLE
Missing parents, file-as-parent, search-mode denial, trailing non-directory paths and exact forty/forty-one link boundaries
Trailing-symlink removal fails and preserves the target directory
Rename, closure of the original Worker, restored read/remove and unchanged unrelated lexical-parent bytes
Existing long lexical symlink targets remain valid persisted v6 manifests

Native WASI lexical floor checks remain conservative; full cross-runtime POSIX descriptor/cwd coherence remains open.

Native kernel/WASI binaries change; existing exact-binary checkpoint compatibility rules apply. Full upstream parity and real Minutei production/model validation remain open.
